sources.entry: faststream - A framework for building async services over Kafka, RabbitMQ, NATS, MQTT, and Redis.

summary.one_liner: FastStream is an asynchronous Python framework for building event-driven services and producers/consumers over Kafka, RabbitMQ, NATS, Redis and MQTT, using FastAPI-style decorators.
summary.what_it_does: Provides @broker.subscriber and @broker.publisher decorators that consume and produce messages on Kafka, RabbitMQ, NATS, Redis and MQTT brokers, handling decoding and encoding automatically. Message bodies are validated and parsed through type annotations, using Pydantic by default or the built-in Msgspec serializer. It generates an AsyncAPI specification from the handlers. An in-memory TestBroker context manager lets tests run subscribers and publishers without a live broker. The faststream CLI runs apps with hot reload and multi-worker options, and a dependency injection system (Depends) supplies handler dependencies. Each broker client wraps its native library, so broker-specific features remain accessible.
use_cases: process RabbitMQ or NATS queue messages
validate incoming JSON messages with Pydantic
generate AsyncAPI docs for message channels
unit test message handlers without a broker
run message consumers alongside an aiohttp or FastAPI app
notable: Same decorator style as FastAPI, applied to message brokers
In-memory TestBroker for tests without containers
Automatic AsyncAPI documentation generated from handlers
Thin wrappers over each broker's native client, with native features still reachable
Built-in Msgspec serializer alternative to Pydantic
caveats: The FastAPI plugin is deprecated and moving to the faststream_fastapi package, to be removed in 1.0.0
Version 1.0 is not yet released; pre-1.0 minor releases may include breaking changes
Each broker requires its own optional install extra
keywords: test kafka consumers without a broker
